purpose: Independent behavioral oracle for coupled Order Filler and ClockTimer states. Named cases cover a subset; absence is unreviewed, never permission or silence.

timing.source: Derived from timestamps and selected goal; not clock_phase alone
timing.notes: B-game: selected goal above 100%, goal deadline passed, before the standard deadline. A startRelation of early is historical and does not imply still before scheduled start. Pauses retain timing context.

sync.notes: Enabled preference and effective active/off/offline/blocked/data-unavailable status are distinct; enumerate separately.

focus.notes: Open surfaces and focused surface are separate. Commands availability also depends on modal context and open collectors.

operation.notes: Owner, operation phase, validation, persistence result, cancellation and stale completion affect transitions.

session.notes: Authentication, permissions and connection constrain actions.

utterance.source: SpeechMenu continuation owner and settlement events
utterance.notes: Root/command/context collection, malformed input, deferred validity and adaptive silence affect command and announcement timing.

appMode.notes: Current implementation explicitly declares debug. No missing-mode fallback. Production and Simulation are reserved future modes, not enabled runtime options. Simulation behavior is unspecified.

invariants.requirement: Four PIN digits plus one OK submit once. There is no second confirmation.
Sleeping admits only Wake and its configured aliases. Pointer access to Commands remains available and does not wake recognition.
Time readbacks do not write trip data and leave no operation locks.
Announcements belong to a transition/request, are not replayed on each tick, and stale owners must not announce.
Unspecified Total is Day and unspecified goals are 100%. Touch and voice can enter Auto without any setup selector or goal editor.

Main standard_time_component is trip-only and its label is Standard Time in every scope. Header edit remains available during a normal active trip, including Down/Break/Lunch; standalone breaks have no standard. Aggregate accounting is unchanged.

Goal-bar Remaining = trip standard minus node counted position. Standard is 0:00 at 100%; Current is 0:00 at counted trip standard. Elapsed uses counted trip time, without prior aggregate elapsed history. End Time for every node, including Current, uses its trip counted position and the existing trip deadline formatter.
Idle nodes use configured goals. Active aggregate nodes use inferred current-trip requirements. Every goal editor edits configured non-inferred values; Standard edits time, not 100%.

Missed labels disappear and goals exit right; all failed retains Standard at right on a zero-to-100% scale with its time and percent details restored. Elapsed color occupies the right segment; all-failed Overtime runs from Current to final failed goal. Down uses its configured color; Break/Lunch colors do not replace productive bar colors.

Circles are opaque and packed using radius plus half each computed stroke width. Borders touch without overlap; miss pulses expand inward. Ticks travel with nodes. Labels have independent collision packing and leaders. Times/percentages share preferred 16px sizing.

Whole bar, including nodes, labels, background and compression triangles, opens the existing selector: Trip only in Trip mode, selected aggregate only in aggregate mode, both in Auto. Failure count does not filter choices. No Standard Time edit or Current time-mode action from the bar. Classic and Bar goal dialogs and pads show actual configured and inferred trip values; only actual is edited.

Above-150 user goal input becomes 150 before UI feedback. Correction sentence precedes recalculation and later chain announcements. Speech-passive notice never takes command ownership; audio batching does not serialize independent command slots.

Drop-In shares rendering and configured-goal selection. Observer permissions remain unchanged; publisher Standard Time is read-only. Raw configured publisher attributes take precedence over inferred UI goal components.

Existing node movement, failure exit, fitting and reduced motion are implemented. Load/start/end choreography is specified in goal-bar.md but remains proposed; do not infer deployed animation states from the specification.
invariants.verificationScope: Documentation status and parity only; lifecycle choreography is proposed, not runtime evidence.

invariants.requirement: Trip mode shows Standard, Trip and active Current; aggregate modes show Standard, selected aggregate and active Current; Auto shows both goal types. Idle follows the same goal visibility without Current. Hidden modes cannot enter bar nodes or goal-selector choices. All active values are trip-based; aggregate goals are inferred trip requirements.

Active main time value exactly matches bar Current in every selected time mode and percentage scope. Remaining = trip standard minus trip counted elapsed. Elapsed = trip counted elapsed. End Time uses Current counted position. Interval annotations and formatters are shared. Goal accounting and idle aggregate summaries remain separate.

Only the next target (highest unfailed visible goal) and Current show times and percentages. Other unfailed nodes retain circles, names; the whole bar opens the goal selector. All-failed retains Standard at the right with its time and 100% reference details, and Current on a zero-to-100% scale.

defaults.rule: Missing Total scope means Day. Missing Trip or Total goal means 100%. Auto proceeds without a scope or percentage setup prompt; explicit settings take precedence.

inventorySemantics: Case families are runtime-test projections, not the exhaustive shared vocabulary. App-mode observations are execution-policy metadata. The shared inventory and Debug-only workflows are in application-state-inventory.json; server-assigned trips are excluded from the current map.

transitional.label: Transitional announcements
transitional.meaning: Feedback or a prompt caused by a workflow/domain state transition, including transitions initiated by voice or touch. Suppress duplicate/no-op transitions and stale transition owners.

user-activated.label: User-activated announcements
user-activated.meaning: Information explicitly requested by the user, such as Time or Trip Summary. Opening an informational surface does not reclassify the response as transitional.

productionRequirements.requirement: Server assigns the next trip and its standard time; summary OK must not open manual standard-time entry.
No assignment must not silently fall back to Debug/manual entry. Waiting/error presentation is to be specified.

simulationRequirements.requirement: Reserve simulation as an explicit app-mode. Define its trip source, timing, persistence, commands and announcements before activation; do not infer these from Debug or Production.
